region: Marsure di Povoletto · Udine, Friuli, Italy
about: Cividina is made by Distillerie Bepi Tosolini, named for its patriarch Giuseppe “Bepi” Tosolini, a Friulian who began distilling in 1943. He built a distillery in Udine in the 1950s and, in 1973, a new one at Marsure di Povoletto, among vineyards in the shadow of the Friulian Alps, close to the Slovenian border. The Tosolini family still owns it, and is credited with helping turn grappa from a rough farm spirit into a refined one.

Grappa is distilled from pomace, the skins and seeds left after winemaking, and Tosolini draws fresh pomace from Friuli’s Collio, Colli Orientali and Grave appellations. Cividina, its name a nod to the Cividale district east of Udine, blends pomace from several Friulian grape varieties and is steam-distilled in traditional copper stills that are run by hand. It is bottled unaged and clear at 40%.

Difford’s Guide finds it clean, fruity and well balanced, with chalky minerality, white pepper and faint florals on the nose, then blanched almond and a peppery finish. Others note softer peach, apricot and citrus-oil tones. Serve it slightly cool in a small tulip glass after dinner, the way it is poured in Friuli, where a glass of grappa traditionally closes the meal.
facts: Pomace from a blend of Friulian grape varieties
